How to stop putting off
the things that matter
Make the first step tiny. Not "write the report" but "open the document and write one sentence." Starting is the hardest part.
Work for just ten minutes. Set a timer and promise yourself you can stop after. Most of the time, you'll keep going.
Do the hardest thing first. Before email, before social media, before anything easy. The rest of the day feels lighter.
Remove the distraction physically. Phone in another room, website blocked, desk cleared. Willpower is weaker than a good setup.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. A small daily habit proves you can follow through on bigger ones.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. A small daily habit proves you can follow through on bigger ones.

slides.texte_overlay: Tell someone your deadline. A friend, a colleague, a partner. Being accountable to someone else makes it much harder to delay.
Forgive yourself for yesterday. Guilt about past delays only creates more delay. Start fresh with the next small step.
